answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybil attacks by tying every seller to one costly, verifiable identity thread. Each agent posts a refundable stake on a public ledger linked to a single hardware-backed credential, so a thousand fake sellers cost a thousand stakes. Reputation then grows only through completed trades, like trees in an orchard maturing season by season: no newcomer can fake years of honest deliveries overnight, and cheating burns stake and reputation together.
